newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: At least 20 killed in combat near Colombian capital.
newsitem.headline: At least 20 killed in combat near Colombian capital.

text.p: At least 20 people have been killed in heavy fighting between the army and leftist rebels in an area just outside the Colombian capital where the fate of dozens of soldiers was unknown late on Monday, authorities said.
They said the fighting, which began on Friday in a mountainous and rugged area of Meta province about 30 miles (50 km) east of Bogota, was the heaviest to erupt near Bogota in recent memory.

The exact toll from the combat, in which troops were backed by helicopter gunships and bombers, was unknown, according to senior military officials. But it brought Colombia's long-running guerrilla war to the doorstep of the capital with dramatic flourish.
The Radionet radio news network said at least 19 soldiers were killed and reported eight others wounded.

There was no official confirmation from the military but army commander Gen. Manuel Jose Bonett told a news conference about 40 soliders were missing in the combat zone and could conceivably be among the dead.
Radio contact with the missing troops, who might also have been taken prisoner, was lost at midday on Sunday.

Teddy Torbeaum, head of the Red Cross in Meta province, told Reuters that members of the International Committee of the Red Cross had counted "at least 20 dead" outside the small town of San Juanito, near where much of the fighting was taking place.
Most of the victims were soldiers but some were also presumed to be guerrillas, Torbeaum said.

San Juanito town Mayor Ramiro Jimenez told national radio that hundreds of peasants from three outlying villages had poured into his town since the weekend, seeking refuge from the combat and aerial bombardments by the military.

The fighting around San Juanito began shortly after Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels in the area released two kidnap victims, a Bogota businessman and French highway engineer Alain Fablet, seized by the FARC in October, army sources said.
